page.layout: One printed page, one text column with marginal reference marks in the right margin. Running head at top, page number at top right. Signature "D 4" at the bottom right, below the last line.

main_text.p: eres liberos præ inedia comederint. Factũ est hoc in obsidione Samariæ, in prima obsidioe ỽrbis Hierosolymitanæ sub Nabuchodono|sore, et in posteriore sub vespasiano et Tito. Sancerreses anno 1573. plusquã famem Sa-guntinam passi sunt, quã plurib. describit idẽ author de Statu Reip. & Relig. in Regno Galliæ li. 10. Quanta hæc miseria sit, omnes præsertim matres, intelligũt. ʒ[?]Exactiorem descriptionem si quis desideret legat Ioseph. de bello Iudaico l.6.c.11. Et Eusebh.hist.Eccles. l.3.c.6. qui hæc ex Iosepho excerpsit: Naucle rus scribit An.649. quarto anno regni Clodo uei tantam annonæ caritatẽ in Gallia fuisse, ut fame & inedia populus absque modo periret. Anno 839. tanta fuit fames, ut matres, fame stipulante, filios comederint.

An.808. Dira quoq; fames uniuersam Germaniam vexauit quo tempore Hatto Mogu-tinus Episcopus nefandum illud facinus in miseros rusticos panē petentes perpetrauit. Vrspergens. scribit magnam famem quæ incidit in An.898. homines se inuicem commedere persuasisse. An.1010. vniuerso ferè terrarum in orbe inaudita fames fuit.

page.notes: The two small marks in the right margin (beside "Sancerreses" and beside "Exactiorem") are reference marks; the first is read as a stylised "ʒ" and the second is not included as a separate note because it could not be read with certainty. The first line of the page is a fragment, the start of a word cut at the page edge ("eres" for "ferres"/"ceres"-type word, read as printed). Possible misprint: "Eusebh" is uncertain and may be "Eusebii" or "Eusebh". Inside the text the printed ligatures "s" have been rendered as plain s throughout.
